I1.quote: The ASAP 2020 HD88 from Micromeritics in USA was used for the low-pressure measurements (up to 1 bar) and the gravimetric analyzer HPVA-100 (VTI Corporation of TA Instruments, USA) was used for the high-pressure measurements (up to 8 MPa).
I1.location: main, p. 4 (printed p. 3), Section 2.3.2 H2 adsorption

I2.quote: Based on the previous experiments that the hydrogen storage capacities at 77K has linear relationship with surface area and micropore volume [1, 5], only AC4, which has the highest SBET and VDR were considered for hydrogen storage analysis.
I2.location: main, p. 5 (printed p. 4), Section 3.2 Hydrogen Storage Performance

I3.quote: The results shown that the hydrogen storage capacity as high as 6.7 wt.% at 4 MPa, and 2.86 wt.% at 1 bar were obtained at 77 K.
I3.location: main, p. 6 (printed p. 5), Section 3.2 Hydrogen Storage Performance

I4.quote: Our lab-made AC has a better hydrogen storage performance because it has higher SBET than Maxsorb-3: 3503 and 3203 m2 g-1, respectively.
I4.location: main, p. 6 (printed p. 5), Section 3.3 Comparison with Maxsorb-3 and Open Literature

I5.quote: Activated carbons (ACs) with controlled microporosity have been developed from oil palm shell and their H2 storage performances been have tested at 77 K.

notes: Page numbers are PDF pages (p. 1 is the IOP cover page). Conference proceedings paper (WOBIC 2017, IOP Conf. Ser.: Mater. Sci. Eng.) with original data, so not_primary does not apply; record has is_retracted false and the PDF shows no retraction notice; the paper does not state that its H2 values were published before. Sorbent AC4 is KOH-activated oil palm shell carbon (activated_carbon); BET by N2 at 77 K (Section 2.3.1; Table 1 gives AC4 SBET 3503 m2/g). Figure 3 (p. 6) axes also give conditions: y 'Hydrogen storage capacities (wt. % at 77 K)', x 'Pressure (bar)' (a) and 'Pressure (MPa)' (b). Internal inconsistency for extraction: 6.7 wt.% at 4 MPa in Section 3.2, Table 2 and Conclusions, but 6.8 wt.% in the Abstract and Section 3.3. High-pressure instrument is called a 'gravimetric analyzer HPVA-100'. Maxsorb-3 values (5.8 wt.% at 4 MPa, 2.1 wt.% at 1 bar) are given in Section 3.3; Section 2.1 says Maxsorb-3 'was used for the sake of comparison'.
